CHENNAI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam president and chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama as the candidates of the party-led Secular Social Justice alliance for the upcoming by-elections to Mathurantagam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies. Both will contest on the TVK Whistle symbol.In an official statement, Vijay urged party functionaries and cadres to work towards a "historic victory" with a "single goal".Maragatham Kumaravel and Sathyabama were elected on AIADMK's Two Leaves symbol in the previous election, defeating candidates from both DMK and TVK. However, they submitted their resignations to Speaker JCD Prabhakar on May 25 and joined TVK shortly after meeting PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna at the Secretariat.Their resignation triggered the current by-polls. They were among the six AIADMK MLAs who switched sides after resigning their post.Leaders of alliance partners, including the Congress, MDMK, VCK, and IUML, met on Wednesday to formally name the coalition and pledge their support, confirming a joint campaign for both constituencies under TVK leadership.

Stephen Curry, the four time NBA champion, might be one of the strongest players and a force to be reckoned with but at home, he has always been a devoted and a present father to the four children he shares with his wife, the popular entrepreneur Ayesha Curry. Amid this, Stephen Curry has reflected on fatherhood.A few years ago, in an interview with POPSUGAR, the Golden State Warriors' star player reflected on fatherhood as he said, "You learn something from them every single day…They give you a reason to wake up in the morning, regardless of whether work is going well or not. Your biggest responsibility, obviously, is being a parent, and it's just so much fun every single day when they change so fast and you're trying to keep up. ”The NBA legend added, “You get to share so many experiences with them and I'm enjoying every minute of it."Stephen Curry continued, "There's something about them that God's put in their life that's going to make them stand out, so embrace whatever that is...As they go through life, that's hopefully what sparks their success."Stephen Curry seems to have a special and an unbreakable bond with each of his four children.Both he and his wife, the popular actress and chef, Ayesha Curry, have always been friendly towards their children and have encouraged them to take up whatever they are interested in, instead of following their father’s path.Stephen Curry seems perfect both on and off the field. While the four time NBA champion has been married to his wife, Ayesha Curry, for over a decade and has been with her since they were young adults, their marriage has always attracted a lot of negative drama.Both Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have been mature enough to ignore it as he has even stood up for her to stop the hate she was receiving from fans.In a recent interview, the NBA icon reflected on his personal life as he said, "You rely on family, for sure. Every year has been a learning lesson when it comes to doing the best we can. Quality time is important and that's when you get the most joy. We really try to protect that at all costs."For now, both Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have built businesses together and remain committed to providing help to their hometown in Oakland.With just a few more weeks left for the new season to begin, Stephen Curry remains busy with training and recovery.

Carlos Alcaraz’s US Open title defence ended in dramatic fashion as Ben Shelton defeated the defending champion in a thrilling five-set quarterfinal. The Spaniard fought back after losing the second and third sets, but could not complete the comeback. Shelton eventually won 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(7) in a match that finished after 2:50am in New York.Alcaraz also left fans concerned when he appeared to vomit into his towel after the fourth set. The 23-year-old had pushed himself through a gruelling contest against Shelton. The physical strain was clear as the match entered a deciding fifth set. Fans quickly reacted online to the extraordinary scenes before Shelton sealed a famous victory.Carlos Alcaraz looked in control early in the match against Ben Shelton. He took the opening set 7-6(5) after a tense tiebreak. However, the American quickly changed the momentum.Shelton dominated the second set and won it 6-1. He then took the third set 6-3 to move within one set of a huge upset.Alcaraz refused to give up. The defending champion raised his level in the fourth set. He raced through it 6-1 and forced a deciding fifth set.But shortly after winning the set, Alcaraz appeared to be sick into his towel during the changeover.The moment immediately caught the attention of fans watching around the world.Alcaraz appeared to turn away from the court as he tried to recover. Former American tennis player James Blake said the Spaniard did not want the camera to show him being sick and asked the cameraman to look away. Despite the difficult moment, Alcaraz continued.Fans had already praised Alcaraz for continuing despite his physical struggles. One fan wrote, “The US Open conditions are brutal. A fan wrote, “Alcaraz x Shelton was a treat for my eyes today”.Shelton held serve at the beginning of the fifth set, putting the Spaniard under immediate pressure. The fifth set eventually went to a deciding tiebreak.Shelton kept his composure and moved closer to one of the biggest wins of his career. He finally completed the upset by winning the tiebreak 10-7. His final blow was a 146mph serve out wide.The result sent Alcaraz out of the US Open and booked Shelton a place in the semi-finals against fellow American Frances Tiafoe.

Article Title: Dana White’s blunt words on Ilia Topuria reveal what could come next for his UFC return
Article Text:
Ilia Topuria (Image via IG/X)

Dana White confirms Ilia Topuria is ready as the UFC waits for his next move

Dana White sees big opportunities in both a Gaethje rematch and a Paddy Pimblett fight

Ilia Topuria’s UFC comeback may be much closer than expected, and Dana White has now given the clearest update yet. The UFC CEO confirmed that the former lightweight champion is ready to return, despite the serious injuries he suffered in his loss to Justin Gaethje. Topuria’s recovery had already created hope that he could fight again before the end of 2026. White’s latest comments take that optimism a step further. The UFC is ready for him, but his next opponent has not been decided. For now, both Gaethje and Paddy Pimblett remain possible options.Dana White has made it clear that the UFC is not holding Topuria back from competition. Speaking to Jim Rome, White explained that the promotion remains in contact with the former champion and is prepared to move forward when the right fight is available."Our guys are always in touch with them. We don't have him on the schedule right now, but listen, Topuria's ready to fight. We're ready for him."That statement is significant because Topuria’s return looked far less certain immediately after his latest fight.The 29-year-old suffered his first professional loss against Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250. The defeat ended his unbeaten run and came with serious physical damage.Reports indicated fractures to both orbital bones, along with injuries to his nose and foot.Those injuries initially raised the possibility of a lengthy absence. A return in 2027 was even discussed.The recovery process, however, has moved faster than expected.Topuria’s strength and conditioning coach Jesus Gallo previously suggested that the former champion could potentially return before the end of 2026. Topuria has also dropped hints about his next appearance, giving fans more reason to believe his comeback is approaching.White’s latest comments now provide the strongest indication yet that the UFC is preparing for that return.The key point is that Topuria does not have a fight officially booked. That leaves the UFC with an important decision over who should welcome him back.Dana White appears to have two major options in mind for Topuria.One is a rematch with Gaethje. The other is a long-awaited showdown with Paddy Pimblett.When Jim Rome asked White which fight he preferred, the UFC CEO did not commit to either matchup."[Justin Gaethje or Paddy Pimblett?] Both sound good to me. They're both great. We don't lose with either one of those fights. They're both great fights; I don't know."A second fight with Gaethje would give Topuria an immediate chance to respond to the biggest setback of his career. Their first meeting was not decided by a controversial scorecard. Gaethje gradually took control before Topuria’s corner stopped the fight ahead of the fifth round.That makes a rematch easy to understand from a storyline perspective. Topuria would have the opportunity to correct what went wrong and show whether he can handle Gaethje differently the second time.Pimblett offers another kind of attraction.The two lightweight stars have built a heated rivalry over several years. Their relationship has included repeated verbal attacks and confrontations, giving a potential fight plenty of tension before the opening bell.White acknowledged that history while discussing the matchup."They're both great; we don't have anything set… I don't really have the answer to that question. I mean, obviously the rematch with Gaethje is incredible. And a Paddy Pimblett fight is amazing. You know, as bad as those two hate each other."There is also a sporting question surrounding the Gaethje rematch. Topuria lost the lightweight title without successfully defending it, while Gaethje has argued that another contender should have a stronger claim to the next championship opportunity.That could make an immediate rematch difficult to justify from a rankings standpoint.Still, White’s comments show that the idea remains alive.For now, the biggest takeaway is not which opponent Topuria will face. It is that the UFC boss believes the former champion is ready to return.Dana White has effectively moved the conversation forward. Topuria’s comeback is no longer simply being discussed as a future possibility. The UFC is preparing for it, and the next decision could determine whether he returns looking for revenge against Gaethje or settles his long-running rivalry with Pimblett.
Article Summary: Dana white confirms ilia topuria is ready to return from injury. Former lightweight champion suffered serious injuries in loss to justin gaethje. Ufc ceo says the promotion is prepared to move forward when the right fight is available. Topuria has dropped hints about his next appearance, giving fans more reason to believe his comeback is approaching.

Article Title: Barry Melrose cause of death: How did the former player, coach and ESPN analyst die at 70
Article Text:
Barry Melrose Dies at 70 (Getty Images)

What was Barry Melrose's cause of death?

How did Barry Melrose build his legacy across playing, coaching and broadcasting?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Barry Melrose, one of the most recognizable faces in hockey broadcasting, died Wednesday at the age of 70. His wife, Cindy, confirmed the passing to ESPN, which broke the news to a hockey world that had not forgotten the man who spent decades shaping how fans understood the sport. Melrose had been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2023, leading to his retirement from ESPN after nearly 30 years with the network. His death drew immediate tributes from across the NHL, the broadcasting world, and beyond.Barry Melrose died following a battle with Parkinson's disease. The illness had already forced him out of public life two years earlier. When he announced his retirement in October 2023, he said: "I've had over 50 extraordinary years playing, coaching and analyzing the world's greatest game, hockey. It's now time to hang up my skates and focus on my health, my family, including my supportive wife Cindy, and whatever comes next. "ESPN did not formally confirm Parkinson's disease as the official cause of death, but the timeline is clear. The diagnosis came just as the 2023-24 NHL season opened, and he never returned to the desk. When ESPN's Steve Levy announced on the eve of the 2023 Stanley Cup Final that Melrose would not continue their long streak of covering the series together, it led many in the hockey community to suspect something was wrong.That suspicion turned out to be correct.Melrose was 67 when he got the diagnosis. He was gone at 70.Melrose finished his NHL playing career with 10 goals, 33 points, and 728 penalty minutes across 300 regular season games. He suited up for the Winnipeg Jets, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Detroit Red Wings. The stats tell you what kind of player he was: hard-nosed, physical, not there to fill up the scoresheet. What he was building, though, was something harder to quantify.As a coach, he took the Wayne Gretzky-led Kings to the precipice of their first Stanley Cup in 1993 in his first season guiding an NHL team. That run was stunning. Los Angeles lost to the Montreal Canadiens in five games, but the Kings had never been there before, and Melrose had gotten them there in year one. He continued coaching the Kings for two more seasons, finishing both years out of the playoffs with losing records. Just 30 minutes after the Kings fired him in April 1995, Melrose was signed by ESPN to work as a studio analyst during the upcoming NHL playoffs. That timing says a lot about how the network saw him.His television career defined him to a new generation of fans. Known for his sense of humor, his mullet, and his fancy suits, Melrose became a star on ESPN, endearing himself to hockey fans everywhere. He had a way of making the game feel approachable without ever dumbing it down.When asked what he wanted viewers to take away from watching him, he told the Los Angeles Times in 1995: "When [people] watch me on TV, I want them to go, 'Geez, I'd like to go for a beer with Barry Melrose and talk hockey. He seems like he'd be very interesting.'"NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman paid tribute after the news broke.ESPN's John Buccigross wrote: "Barry was my best friend at ESPN. A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting — the rink was Barry's home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever. "
Article Summary: Barry melrose, one of the most recognizable faces in hockey broadcasting, died wednesday at the age of 70. Melrose had been diagnosed with parkinson's disease in 2023, leading to his retirement from espn after nearly 30 years with the network. His death drew immediate tributes from across the nhl, the broadcasting world, and beyond.

Article Title: Varun Chakravarthy's second act: Why India's mystery spinner still believes he's only halfway through his career
Article Text:
India's Varun Chakaravarthy (Image: IANS)

Learning a new kind of injury

Why shoes matter more than mystery

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most important trait for a T20 cricketer? Adaptability. Aggression. Consistency. Strategy. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The curiosity beyond cricket

NEW DELHI: For a cricketer who made his international debut at 29, Varun Chakravarthy measures time differently.Now, at 35, he has just lived through a rollercoaster year: a T20 World Cup title on home soil where he finished as India's joint-highest wicket-taker with 14 wickets, an IPL campaign played through hairline fractures in his left hand and toe, and then the first muscle injury of his career that forced him into weeks of rehabilitation.Yet, ask him where he stands in his journey, and his answer is strikingly uncomplicated."At this stage of my career, I still feel I'm in my first half of my career because I started cricket very late. So I still feel there's a long way to go," Chakaravarthy said in an interaction with TimesofIndia.com, facilitated by equipment manufacturer ASICS.It is an outlook that perhaps explains Chakravarthy's unconventional rise better than any statistic. The Tamil Nadu spinner has never been one for grand declarations or five-year plans. In a sport as volatile as T20 cricket, he prefers chasing the next small improvement rather than the next milestone.Now fully recovered from the Grade 2 left hamstring injury he suffered during the England T20I series, Chakravarthy returns just in time for a busy stretch: three T20Is against Afghanistan, a historic one-off international against Japan, and the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, where defending champions India begin directly from the quarterfinals.Until this summer, pain had always arrived the same way for Chakravarthy, through collisions, impact or bad luck.A torn muscle was unfamiliar territory."This is actually my first ever muscle injury. So all of my injuries have been impact injuries and other accidents that have happened on field. The expertise at CoE helped me and people helped me to gain my confidence. Every person working there helped me," he explained.Recovery meant long days at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, where rebuilding confidence became as important as rebuilding strength. The rehabilitation, too, was relentless."Definitely, I spent a lot of time there and did a lot of running and did a lot of strength training, which helped me."For a bowler whose craft depends on rhythm as much as deception, returning isn't simply about being medically fit. It's about trusting the body enough to express the imagination that makes him so difficult to read."Yeah, it will take some time to gain confidence. But once you gain confidence, you just start becoming more expressive and that's how it is," reasoned the 35-year-old.Rather than treating injury lay-offs as wasted time, Chakravarthy sees them as opportunities to work on parts of the game that competition rarely allows."When you're away, you can start sharpening your skills. You can upskill yourself, which you don't get much time to do when you're playing continuously."Mystery spin is often associated with wrists, fingers and release points. Chakravarthy begins somewhere else entirely: the feet.His partnership with ASICS may be commercial, but his relationship with the brand predates the endorsement. He says he had already switched to their shoes around 2022 before formally signing a deal in January 2026.More revealing is how clinically he breaks down footwear."For a bowler, shoes are the biggest equipment they can have. Batters, they have many other equipments, but for a bowler, it's the shoes only," said Varun."As a spinner, your feet start becoming little broader as in it starts changing shape once you pivot because the spinners have to pivot more after landing. So broad shoes in the toe area that is very important," he added.Add a supportive heel counter and lighter weight, he says, and you've got the essentials of a spinner's toolkit.It's the kind of detail that reflects Chakravarthy's evolution from architect to elite cricketer: analytical, process-driven and constantly searching for marginal gains.The Asian Games, which begin on September 19, offer something even ICC events cannot — a sporting village shared with athletes from dozens of disciplines. For Chakravarthy, that might be the biggest attraction."It's my first time in Japan. I've never been to Japan and any games also. So all I've played is ICC tournaments and ACC tournaments," said Chakravarthy, his excitement quite evident in his voice."I'm very much looking forward to meeting other athletes also from other different sports and all those things.""I want to see how a 100-metre athlete prepares himself, how a badminton professional prepares himself or herself," he went on to state.In India's increasingly packed cricket calendar, opportunities for cross-pollination are rare. The Asian Games provide a window into sporting cultures that cricketers seldom experience.That openness may also prove useful on the field. The pitches at Korogi Sports Park are expected to differ from familiar Indian surfaces, and Chakravarthy believes adaptability will define the bowling attack's success more than preconceived plans

He says he had already switched to asics shoes around 2022 before formally signing a deal in january 2026. So broad shoes in the toe area that is very important," said chakravarthy.

Article Title: Noah Lyles eyes 2028 Olympic title defence after injury ends season
Article Text:
Noah Lyles of United States (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Noah Lyles wasn’t planning on playing ‘commentator’ ahead of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship.The reigning men’s Olympic 100m champion had been looking forward to joining the sport’s biggest stars at World Athletics’ new season-ending showpiece in Budapest, until injury forced him to end his season early.In a video call with reporters on Tuesday, Lyles grinned when he was asked a couple of times for his views on some of his rivals who will be in action this weekend. “Shoot, I usually focus more on myself than other people,” Lyles said in response to a question about his American compatriot Kenny Bednarek attempting the sprint double in Budapest. When the very next question was about what impression he had of some of the South African sprinters, the 29-year-old smiled again while going on to say, “I’m not here to be a commentator of sorts today. That’s not really my goal.”And then came a question about 2027. The conversation was about Noah Lyles once again. And the four-time 200m world champion was only too happy to look ahead to what he considers the ‘building blocks’ in his quest to defend his Olympic 100m crown on home soil in Los Angeles.“I am very excited for 2027. It’s going to be a lot of fun,” Lyles said. “2027 is the building block for 2028. And let’s get that plan smooth and polished so that when we go into 2028, we’re just following the blueprint because we know it’s going to work.”Though he sustained his season-ending injury at the US nationals in July, Lyles managed to run two 9.7-second races at the event before the setback, leaving even himself a little ‘shocked’.“I don’t like to put limits on myself,” Lyles said. “In my head, American records definitely come in touching the stars, going after anything and everything. I think I kind of shocked myself a little bit by running those two 9.7s at the nationals because although I was prepared to run fast, I wasn’t prepared to do it then.“So it’s proven to myself that I can run very fast, even though I’m not 100% perfect with my first 30 (metres), which was a super exciting thing. So there’s a lot more to come for 2027 and 2028.”The competitive absence of Lyles is undoubtedly a blow to an event World Athletics has billed as ‘the best of the best’ with a record $10m prize purse on offer. But there’s still a lot on the programme to keep athletics fans hooked, the 1500m race in particular one of the event’s top attractions, seeing as it is set to reignite the rivalry between Great Britain’s Josh Kerr and Norway’s Jakob Ingebrigtsen.Ingebrigtsen’s recent criticism of Kerr for skipping the European Championships last month may well have added a layer of spice to their upcoming showdown. “Always under criticism,” Kerr, who clocked 3:42.66 in the mile at the London Diamond League in July to break Hicham El Guerrouj’s 27-year-old world record, said with a wry chuckle in response to his fierce rival’s comments.“Every person is different, and every athlete is different in the way that they approach the season. For me, the way that I approach it is circling two to four big dates and working my way around those and also to get in and out of a year without massive problems,” added the Scot, who won the 1500m gold at the 2023 world championships in Budapest.
Article Summary: Olympic 100m champion had been looking forward to joining the sport’s biggest stars at world athletics’ new season-ending showpiece in budapest. The 29-year-old smiled when he was asked a couple of times for his views on some of his rivals who will be in action this weekend.

BENGALURU: It was a different day, a different set of fixtures and a different proposition for each team looking to seal a top-two berth. But what remained the same was Viswanathan Anand’s miserable run at the 2026 Global Chess League (GCL) on Wednesday at The Lalit Ashok Hotel. This time, the defeat came against veteran Grandmaster Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, who had White pieces.Although Anand’s side, Alaskan Knights, ended up winning the match against MVL’s Mumba Masters, the Indian legend, still winless with five defeats from seven games, has endured a complicated outing despite producing competitive performances and showing glimpses of brilliance on the "Icon" board against some of the strongest players in the field.After the match, fellow Indian Grandmaster and Anand's teammate Arjun Erigaisi spoke to the media about the veteran's difficult run and why his results do not tell the whole story.Asked about Anand’s recent lack of form on the board, Arjun replied, “At this age, I cannot imagine how many people would be playing at this level. Even though he lost some games, it wasn't like he was getting outplayed or something.”Arjun stressed that Anand, now 56, continues to compete on equal terms with a younger generation of players.“He is still competing head-on with most of these young players. Only in the final moments, some unfortunate things are happening,” he added. “It's hugely inspiring to see how well he is playing at this age.”The 23-year-old also discussed the conversations players have away from the board, particularly after wins and losses, and how they deal with mistakes.“Just analyse the important things that happened and try to rectify whatever can be done,” he revealed. “For example, I was missing a lot of basic tactics in earlier games. His win helped the Alaskan Knights seal the match and also earned Mishra the Player of the Match award. And despite MVL beating Anand and draws on the other three boards, Mumba Masters missed the golden opportunity to showcase their authority on the points table.Earlier in the day, APL Pipers strengthened their position with an 11-6 win over Mumba Masters, while Ganges Grandmasters thrashed Triveni Continental Kings 15-3.In the final match on Wednesday, American Gambits edged Triveni Continental Kings 8-5 to move to the top of the standings.

Article Title: Who are Drew Lock’s parents? Meet Andy and Laura Lock, the family behind the Seattle Seahawks QB
Article Text:
Who are Drew Lock’s parents? Meet Andy and Laura Lock, the family behind the Seattle Seahawks QB(Instagram)

Who are Drew Lock’s parents, Andy and Laura Lock?

How Drew Lock’s parents supported him throughout his NFL journey

Drew Lock has stepped back into the spotlight for the Seattle Seahawks after Sam Darnold was ruled out with a hip injury during the season opener against the Patriots. Lock entered the game as Seattle’s backup quarterback and took over for Darnold. But behind his long football journey are two people who have been there from the beginning: his parents, Andy and Laura Lock.Both of Drew’s parents had sporting backgrounds of their own, and they played a major role in helping him develop as an athlete and as a person. While Andy had experience as a college football player, Laura was a standout basketball player who later worked in education.Drew was born in Columbia, Missouri, on November 10, 1996, and grew up in Lee’s Summit. He was raised by Andy and Laura on their 10-acre family homestead, where sports became a big part of his childhood.Andy had played offensive tackle for the Missouri Tigers from 1986 to 1989. He went undrafted after college but received an opportunity to attend New York Giants training camp after his playing career at Missouri. His football career did not last long, but he later built a career in business. A LinkedIn profile previously cited in reporting listed Andy as a regional manager with the McCormick and Schmidt’s franchise in Lee’s Summit from 2005.Laura grew up in Centralia, Missouri, and was a star high school basketball player. She later worked as a teacher and school administrator. Her own experience in sports helped her understand the demands placed on a young athlete, although she was also closely involved in Drew’s life away from competition.Andy and Laura met at a bank in Columbia. Laura was working there as a teller when Andy came in to make deposits for a restaurant where he was working after his time with the Giants. Their meeting eventually led to marriage and the birth of Drew and his sister Claire.Laura has recalled how athletic Drew was from a very young age. He played basketball, baseball and other sports while growing up, and his parents encouraged him to develop his abilities without becoming too focused on his own success.Laura was one of Drew’s biggest supporters, particularly when he faced criticism. During the 2020 COVID-19 controversy involving the Denver Broncos, she publicly defended her son and explained that Drew and the quarterback room had asked for permission to watch film at the team facility.Drew later described his mother as a “fiery” person and acknowledged that she would always stand up for him. He also joked about how strongly she reacted when he did not play well.His parents were equally emotional supporters during his college career at Missouri. Laura admitted that watching Drew take hits as a freshman was difficult for her. She recalled sitting in the stands, covering her eyes and hoping he would get back up. After games, Drew would reassure her that he was fine.The quarterback has also spoken about how much it meant to have Andy and Laura attend his games. After one of his early NFL victories, Lock said, “It means the world to me that they end up coming to all these games for me.” He added that they had supported him throughout college and would continue trying to do the same in the NFL.Laura also tried to keep Drew humble as his football career grew. She encouraged him to be thankful for his abilities and to help the people around him rather than boasting about his own achievements.Now, with Lock back on the field for Seattle, his parents remain an important part of the story behind the quarterback. Andy gave him an understanding of the highs and disappointments of football, while Laura provided the constant support and encouragement that followed him from childhood to the NFL.
Article Summary: Drew lock was born in columbia, missouri, on november 10, 1996, and grew up in lee’s summit. He was raised by andy and laura on their 10-acre family homestead. Andy had experience as a college football player, while laura was a standout basketball player who later worked in education.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal challengers bengaluru (rcb) beat chennai super kings (csk) in ipl 2026 encounter at the m chinnaswamy stadium. Tim david, rajat patidar and devdutt padikkal hit 70, 48 and 50 respectively to lift rcb to 250/3. Bhuvneshwar kumar took 3-41 as csk were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs.
